Subject: Deployment options recap + follow-ups (LegacyBank)

Hi Alice / Rajesh —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary goal: move ML inference for transaction scoring into a private, air-gapped environment to meet regulatory controls.
- Preference: on-prem private deployment (no outbound internet from inference hosts).
- Constraints: strict upgrade windows, hardware already planned (we discussed GPUs), need for offline key management, and quarterly maintenance windows.

Open questions we promised to follow up on (see line items below) — if you can confirm, we can scope the technical work and timelines: 
1) Hardware specs: exact GPU model(s) planned (A100 v3, A40, etc.), node counts, and NVMe sizing per node.
2) Upgrade/patch cadence: how often can your team accept downtime for node-level upgrades vs. rolling upgrades?
3) Network constraints: will the inference hosts be fully air-gapped (no outbound) or will they allow egress to a management subnet/VPN only?
4) Ops responsibilities: who applies OS/kernel/driver updates and firmware updates?
5) KMS: do you need on-prem KMS/HSM integration or can you accept a customer-managed remote KMS behind a VPN?

Attachments: I’ll send our private-deployment checklist and a short overview of how Redwood handles offline upgrades and packaging.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm the items above (hardware and ops) — reply inline if easier.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with our Solutions Engineer (Dev) to walk through offline upgrade packaging and compatibility testing.
- After that call we’ll provide a draft deployment plan and timeline.

Would you be available for a 45-minute technical call on Fri Mar 6 or Mon Mar 9 (PST)?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the helpful recap. A few notes / answers below, and I’ve attached our network diagram and the internal checklist you can reference.

Answers to your questions:
1) Hardware: planned initial deployment is 4 nodes with NVIDIA A100 80GB (DGX-style), each node with 4x GPUs (so 16 GPUs total). NVMe per node: 4TB. We may scale to 8 nodes in phase 2.
2) Upgrade/patch cadence: We have quarterly maintenance windows. For the initial rollout we can do a two-week window for system bring-up; ongoing upgrades must be scheduled into quarterly windows. We generally prefer rolling upgrades but can accommodate short full-cluster downtime for major changes.
3) Network: Hosts are fully air-gapped for outbound traffic — no internet egress. We can allow a management VLAN that has controlled, one-way access to a bastion for updates, but only via approved secure channels.
4) Ops responsibilities: Our infra team will own OS-level patching and firmware; we expect Redwood to provide curated offline upgrade bundles and instructions.
5) KMS: We require on-prem HSM integration (FIPS 140-2) and cannot rely on cloud KMS.

Additional asks:
- Can Redwood provide an offline installer bundle (tar + checksums + signed manifests) that can be applied without outbound connectivity?
- How do you manage model or runtime CVE patches in an air-gapped environment — do you provide hotfix bundles or do you require a full offline re-install?

Attached: network_arch_diagram.pdf, legacybank-onprem-checklist.xlsx

Happy to hop on the call Friday if Dev is available.

Best,
Alice Zhang
Head of ML Infrastructure | LegacyBank
alice.zhang@legacybank.com

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the clear answers and the attachments — very helpful. Short answers below and a few clarifying questions so Dev and I can scope the technical plan: 

Yes, we support on-prem, air-gapped deployments and have an offline installer workflow. That said, there are a few details we need to confirm to ensure a smooth rollout: 

Follow-up qualification items (please confirm where possible):
- Exact GPU drivers / CUDA versions you plan to standardize on. If you have an internal image spec, plz share.
- Expected inference QPS and peak concurrent sessions per node (ballpark is fine) so we size batching and KV cache.
- Storage IO profile: mostly read-heavy model artifacts, or heavy write telemetry?
- Certificate management: will you accept our signed manifests for offline installers, and who will verify signatures internally?
- Support model for urgent CVE backports: do you require on-site engineers for critical patches or will secure file transfer + runbook suffice?

What we will provide before the technical call:
- A draft offline installer bundle and verification steps (signed manifest + SHA256 checksums).
- Our recommended node-level configuration (driver versions, kernel tweaks, NVMe layout).
- A runbook for quarterly patching and a rollback plan for emergency hotfixes.

Next step: Dev, can you confirm availability for a 45-min technical deep-dive on Fri Mar 6 at 10:00 AM PST? If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and share our private deployment docs in advance.

Thanks — looping Ben to surface commercial options (Dedicated vs Private on-prem) so we can align pricing and timelines.

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
